#4103. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

#4102. Xbox Vs. PS5: GTA 6 Specs Revealed, And These Are The Biggest Differences

"Pushing both platforms to their absolute limits"

Rockstar Games has today lifted the lid on a bunch of specs for both the Xbox and PS5 versions of GTA 6, revealing some of the biggest differences (and similarities) between playing the game on each platform.

The most notable bit of information is that every single console runs the game at 30FPS. Regardless of whether you're playing on Xbox Series S, Xbox Series X, PS5 or even PS5 Pro, the max you're getting is 30 frames per-second.

"Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants."

There will obviously be resolution differences between each platform, but Rockstar has yet to reveal these details. Expect the Series S to fare the worst, the PS5 Pro to fare the best, and the Series X and PS5 to be pretty much equal.

Rockstar does say that GTA 6 "plays best" on PS5 though (and let's not forget that Sony appears to have a marketing deal in place with Rockstar Games for this release), highlighting the differences between the PS5 and Xbox versions as being "high-fidelity haptic feedback" for the PS5 DualSense controllers, improved spatial audio rendering, and bizarrely, improved load times. That last one is surely just a minimal advantage at best!

Grand Theft Auto VI for PS5 includes high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D Audio, and improved load times, making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

Beyond that, the PS5 Pro version will benefit from improved clarity via PSSR along with ray-traced shadows.

However, the Xbox version has one massive benefit in the form of Xbox Cloud Gaming. It seems Xbox will be the only platform offering cloud streaming for GTA 6 at launch, making it an exclusive of sorts - at least for now. The bizarre bit is that it only appears to be for consoles, rather than other devices like PCs and mobiles.

The Xbox and PS5 versions will also support Remote Play (allowing you to cast your game to another device from your console). Nothing has been said about Quick Resume yet on Xbox, but we assume it'll be supported as well.

Ultimately, GTA 6 is bound to run great regardless of whether you buy it on Xbox or PlayStation, and the "plays best on PS5" differences mentioned by Rockstar Games appear to be minor advantages rather than major ones.

We can't wait for footage to start appearing online next week — especially for the Xbox Series S version — and here's hoping it's going to live up to the ridiculous hype that's been fueling the past decade. Not long to wait at all now!

#4101. Trails beyond the Horizon Sequel Confirmed for 2027 as Falcom Steps Back from Remakes

The next game in Falcom's long running Trails series will be a sequel to Trails beyond the Horizon.

The developer confirmed this in its annual financial report, putting to rest mass speculation from fans of the franchise.

First released in 2024 in Japan, Trails beyond the Horizon features world-shifting story revelations and ends on one hell of a cliffhanger. Its sequel should, finally, have all of the answers — and it's set to launch before the end of September 2027.

The wait hasn't been quite so bad for western players, as Horizon was localised back in January of this year.

However, it should be noted that Falcom's report only refers to the sequel's Japanese release.

It'll be up to western publisher NIS America to work out whether a global launch is feasible, but I'd be shocked if it's not on the cards, because this is the first time in history that the west is actually fully caught up on the series.

Of course, this also means that Falcom is stepping back from its remakes for the time being. After the huge success of Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter and Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, there was a suggestion that the studio would simply follow the money, and go straight into remaking Trails in the Sky the 3rd.

But it's no secret that the developer is ramping up towards the end of Trails as a whole — and so it's prioritising the next step in the franchise's current saga.

Falcom says that Horizon's sequel is the only major title it has in the works for 2027. As such, it's highly likely that its next remake will be targeting a 2028 release.

With all of this in mind, we should be getting our first look at Horizon's sequel in the coming months.

What are your hopes and dreams for the next Trails game? Go beyond the horizon in the comments section below.

#4100. "There’s always a night when Rome burns": South Of Midnight director says that Xbox funding it was "unsustainable", at least in hindsight

"I didn’t know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it"

Compulsion Games parted ways with former owners Xbox, having landed on the long list of things Microsoft were determined to ditch as part of multi-round mass cuts this year. Now, South of Midnight creative director David Sears has suggested that an eventual pulling of the rug was something he feared throughout the game's development, to the point where he seemingly doesn't think he'd have funded it if he'd been in the shoes of Xbox execs.

In an interview with MinnMax, Sears - who left Compulsion in March 2025 - outlined that ideally games big publishers put out aim to fall into one of two buckets. They either make lots of money or increase the prestige of the brand by becoming cultural touchstones across multiple generations. Obviously doing both is the perfect outcome, but Sears pegged South of Midnight as being more geared towards the latter camp. The likes of Double Fine's Keeper and Obsidian's Pentiment are other games which off the top of my head could be said to fit that same mold. The issue, of course, is that when push comes to shove, it's the games which can show a strong bottom line at any given moment which make the best case for their studios' short term survival if cash is tight.

So, South of Midnight lived in a risky place, with Sears recalling: "I literally told people. I was like, yeah, this could be terrible because somebody is going to say, one day, 'The money tap, we're closing those floodgates' and that's going to have really traumatic results downstream". The interviewer then asked Sears if what he was getting at is that, while he's glad Xbox funded South of Midnight, he might not have done so or at least cut the funding earlier if he was in charge of the console maker.

"Yeah, probably," Sears replied. "I mean, I wanted to make it. No doubt. Obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else's money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, because I'm not completely selfless. It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable. So, of course, it was going to have a 'shocking' outcome. I mean, it's easy to dissect it now, right? But at the time, I would talk to other directors and [they] would be like, 'How is this happening? I mean, how did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like, 'For now'. There's always a night when Rome burns and I didn't know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Notably, Sears added that in his view modern Microsoft showed a "more humane" side than the version of the company that existed in the 90s and early 2000s by giving studios like Compulsion a chance to spin out on their own rather than simply shuttering them outright once they were deemed surplus to requirements.

Given the director's no longer at Compulsion, it seems he'll not have a say on what their next game looks like, but as a newly indie studio one would imagine they'll have a keen eye on the bottom line.

#4099. Random: Yes, Young Link Is Still Quicker When He Rolls About In Ocarina's Remake

As many fans begin to wrap up their first play sessions of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, more attention is slowly shifting to the game's speedrunning community.

During the Zelda Direct, Mr. Aonuma noted how child Link's new "dash" ability had been introduced in the remake because many players in the original game would often roll from one point to another. While it is definitely a faster option than walking, it turns out rolling is still a slightly quicker way to get to your destination (at least as Young Link) in the remake.

Speedrunners have now time-trialled Young Link dashing and rolling across Hyrule on the Switch 2, and if you roll about, you should arrive at your location sooner. And hey, every second counts when it comes to speedrunning!

Zelda speedrunning channel 'Kethnaldo' took a closer look, and between running (dashing) and rolling, the real winner here is the technique referred to as "forward hop roll-cancelling", which in one demonstration sees the player run from Koriki Forest to Hyrule Castle and arrive at the castle roughly four seconds earlier than other methods.

"After you front hop, you can roll immediately and get rid of that end lag...so all you're doing is target forward hopping to get that insane momentum, rolling immediately to get rid of all of the end lagging, and then front hopping again as soon as possible to maximise that front hop speed, and you just chain them together as best as you can...you will mess up, but even with mess ups...it's about roughly four seconds faster than running."

So if you want to speed things up when you're on foot as Young Link, rolling is still recommended. And if you can nail the other technique, you'll be shaving quite a bit off the adventure. Of course, keep in mind, this isn't the original Zelda: Ocarina of Time, so there's always a chance Nintendo could make subtle or major adjustments to game mechanics in future game updates.

#4098. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#4097. Arc Raiders devs Embark insist that using genAI for voice lines was necessary, as "actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"

Despite taking the voice performances of actors and feeding them into machines to spurt out AI-generated mimicry, Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg insists that "we are not in the industry of replacing actors." In a new video posted to the Arc Raiders channel focused on audio design, Strandberg refers back to the infamous use of genAI in Arc Raiders to generate voice lines based on real voice actors' performances, something which the game was heavily (and rightly) criticised for before and since its release.

In that linked piece (thanks Oisin!), CEO Patrick Söderlund stated that they have been replacing lines that were originally generated with actual recorded lines, presumably because Arc Raiders has made quite a bit of money and now they feel that they can continue paying actors to record more lines, rather than just scraping their talents and avoiding the dreaded fee of paying professionals for their work. This choice already came after their previous game, The Finals, was heavily criticised for the exact same thing, which is just a fascinating series of decisions to consider.

In the video, audio director Bence Pajor explains that the apparent reason for the use of AI was to avoid the "stress" of having to work around actors' availability, as they may be busy working on other projects when Embark decides that a new feature needs new voice lines recorded. Pings, quests, and in-level mission briefings were thus generated using training data based on existing actors' recordings, saving the need to actually get anyone back in a studio or pay them for their time. Citing the amount of variables that the ping system creates, Pajor claims it "becomes too impractical to record every possible version of something. The actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that", which is a take that falls apart if you consider the simple fact that games of this scope (or bigger) have been managing to work around actors' availability for as long as genAI has not been an accessible technology, which has been almost all of the time that video games have existed. Isn't it crazy that games like Disco Elysium and Baldur's Gate 3 had so, so much recorded dialogue, all without genAI? Or fellow live service shooter Apex Legends, which has been adding and adjusting voice lines via updates for years? How could they possibly have managed it?

Voice actresses Jo Rideout and Diana Gardner, who play Shani and Celeste respectively, are also featured speaking on their characters' relationships as well as their experience working within this hybrid model of recording and generating voices. Gardner notes that "if they only need an hour of my time for a couple call-outs that are short, then I don't have to cancel other shoots or some other project that might also be interesting. So in that way, I feel quite good about it." She then explains that "the contract seemed fair…so it was a no-brainer in that sense. But I didn't know what to expect once I heard the voice come out. I was like, 'Can I take ownership for the performance?' This is hours of work that I've put in, but can I take ownership for the final product? No."

Strandberg goes on to elaborate on his comment on not replacing actors by saying that "We are not in the industry of replacing actors, actually, I think quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance, and we should give them more space." While Embark's audio team are indeed working on replacing the generated lines with actual performances, that doesn't change the fact that the choice to use AI in the first place was one made simply to save money in not paying actors for their specific work and get the game out the door faster — effectively the 'we'll fix it in post' of games development. While I can respect Garner's awareness that it means she can prioritise other projects when necessary, there is that notable tinge of regret in not being able to take ownership for her hours of work. Fundamentally, Embark has demonstrated its willingness to cut talent to cut costs, seemingly happy to post PR videos implying they had no choice due to the game's scope, and that isn't something a company just goes back on once they realise how 'efficient' it can be.

#4096. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#4095. Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic's next DLC is set to expand the city building sim into the one place not corrupted by capitalism: SPACE

Following not the inherent liberal capitalistic framework of city builders like SimCity but instead a revolutionary (sorry) interpretation of planning and logistical simulation that prioritises centralisation and minute detail, Hooded Horse and 3DIVISION's Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic offers a tense, socialist look at what a citybuilder could be. Fellow contributor Sin Vega, in her 1.0 review, described it like this: "You have to build things to demolish things. That might be Workers & Resources in a nutshell. You're not managing budgets (money is exclusively for imports/exports), you're organising stuff." Now, having previously expanding out of the Soviet Republic and across the globe with the World Maps DLC, the next step for socialist citybuilding is, of course, space. Our Edwin outright predicted this two years ago, correctly calling that "the logical endgame here is to go to space." Good on him.

The Space Program DLC, set to release on November 23rd, will add a variety of new technologies and types of industry to the builder. It looks like it'll focus on not only the actual rockets that get into space, and the spectacle of it all, but also the huge amounts of science and industry that get to the point of rockets not exploding upon takeoff. For example, while it's all well and good for Space Program's scientists to be able to design rockets that are capable of remaining together for long enough to land safely, the designs they dream of still have to be built, meaning that industrial pipelines must be effectively centralised to ensure that every single component is of high quality and arriving in the required quantity.

The update also specifies the Sputnik and Vostok programs as elements of the expansion, implying a close historical aspect to it — though, elsewhere, "an unprecedented duel with nature" is mentioned, which is referring to either the simple harshness of space or aliens. Jury's out. A 1960s campaign will be a star feature of the DLC, which is described as a place for players to learn the new mechanics "in relative peace, surrounded by a happy, healthy, and economically stable utopia." What an idea.

#4094. Try Hellraiser: Revival in This New PS5 Demo, Out Now

Saber Interactive is letting you sample the opening moments of Hellraiser: Revival via a new PS5 demo that's been put on the PS Store today. This isn't one that's tied to PS Plus Premium; it's a free download for everyone.

You'll get to play through the game's prologue, and then a "portion" of the first chapter. This means you'll get to see a lot of what the title is all about: gore, action, sex... and more gore. The first hour or so lets you enter the Labyrinth, and then chapter one is more of a stealth sequence where you have to escape your captors.

Since the demo breaks up a piece of the full game, I don't believe that your progress would carry over if you were to buy it afterwards. Still, it's a nice sample of a horror game I had a lot of fun with a few weeks ago.

If you like what you play, Hellraiser: Revival is full price at the moment: £34.99 / $39.99 on the PS Store. I expect the game will go on sale at some point before the year is out, though, so it might be worth waiting and keeping an eye on our coverage of the PS Store sales to come.

#4093. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

#4091. I'm sad that the Like A Dragon creator's new studio is closing, but I wish their now-cancelled debut Gang of Dragon wasn't just LAD again

Less than a year after the announcement of their first game, and only four years after the studio's creation, Gang of Dragon developers Nagoshi Studio have been dissolved by a shareholders' resolution (thanks, Gematsu.) That also means a premature end for Gang of Dragon, which was announced at last year's Game Awards with a flashy trailer featuring Like a Dragon-esque realistic visuals, combat and exploration through Kabukicho, a couple new elements like actual gunplay and car chases, as well as the star power of actor Ma Dong-seok (a.k.a. Don Lee). Following reports in March that NetEase, the studio's source of funding, would be pulling said funding in May due to ballooning costs reaching around seven billion yen, the time has sadly come for Nagoshi Studio, having not found any alternative funding sources in the time since.

Gang of Dragon looked very much to be 'just Like a Dragon again', which I find to be something of a depressing fate for a studio headed by the original series' creator. Having left Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio following Judgment and Yakuza: Like a Dragon, two of its most innovative games both with new protagonists and one entirely new turn-based gameplay style, it feels indicative of the industry that Nagoshi was granted funding seemingly on the condition that the studio makes something that just looks like the rest of the Like a Dragon series. I love Ma Dong-seok as an actor, but his presence was one of the more blatant, 'look, we got that guy!' castings of the LAD archetype, which is saying something considering Infinite Wealth had fucking Danny Trejo in a prominent role. The trailer closing with a shot of Dong-seok framed by Kabukicho's torii gate, maybe the most famous image from the Like a Dragon series, put a sour taste in my mouth as being just more of the same brand recognition (yet, for a new IP!) to prioritise safe return on investment.

I'm unfortunately not that surprised to see Gang of Dragon and Nagoshi Studio lost to time, though I am sad about it. I have some conflicted feelings on Nagoshi as a person/auteur, but I don't think he, or his studio, deserves to have funding pulled before they could even release anything as a result of NetEase deciding to pull investments out of non-Chinese companies over time. It's unknown what Nagoshi and the team will be attempting next, but I truly hope they can eventually make something. No More Heroes studio Grasshopper Manufacture was able to detach themselves from NetEase very recently and possibly avoid a similar fate, so it might not be impossible.

#4090. Xbox CEO Issues Statement On GTA 6 And New '10-Year Partnership' With Its Publisher

The game is also now the most pre-ordered Microsoft Store title ever

We're getting a whole ton of GTA 6 details coming out today, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has taken to social media to issue a statement about the game's pre-orders, as well as a new 10-year partnership with its publisher Take-Two.

Sharma didn't share any specific details about the partnership in her post, but we did cover the deal at the beginning of October, which allows Take-Two to develop and sell Xbox-compatible products across all Xbox devices. The Xbox boss did also highlight that GTA 6 has now set a record for the most pre-orders of any Microsoft Store / Xbox Store game in history.

It's no surprise that the most anticipated game of all time is picking up its fair share of pre-orders ahead of launch. The numbers were looking good as early as August, when Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick described GTA 6's pre-orders as "unprecedented and astonishing".

Of course, Zelnick wasn't talking solely about Xbox's pre-order total, but it's great to see Sharma commenting on Microsoft's numbers specifically.

Beyond handling Rockstar's GTA and Red Dead Redemption IPs, Take-Two Interactive also manages 2K and Zynga titles. If Sharma intends to entertain more than a billion players every day, striking up a cloud streaming deal with Take-Two is a great place to start.

#4089. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel teaser all but confirms Hammerfell setting and means we can finally stop using that eight year old header image with the hills

Say hello to sandy scroll screengrab for the foreseeable future

Praise Talos and whatever other Elder Scrolls deities you might worship. We here at RPS and in the wider gaming press finally have new material to use when hunting for images to symbolise The Elder Scrolls 6. No more will we be limited to that shot of some hills from the 2018 teaser, because Bethesda have shown off an elder scroll covered in sand while revealing the new game's subtitle and all but locking in a setting. As a recent report from The Verge claimed, it's called The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel and looks to be set in Hammerfell.

These details were revealed in a short teaser at the end of a Todd Howard-fronted video celebrating Bethesda Game Studios' 40th anniversary. As such, the majority of the video is the Toddinator recapping the studio's history by touching on each of the games they've put out since 1986's Gridiron. Then, he looks to the future. "You know, everybody’s always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," the Toddfather said. "And we thought, hey, given the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called."

Cue a shot of an elder scroll buried in sand, followed by the The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel in fancy logo font. Then, a quote attributed to a moth priest called Yazar. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate." OOH, CRYPTIC. In all seriousness, between the subtitle, the sand, and Yazar being referred to as a moth priest in service of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, the Verge report's assertion that the game will be set in Hammerfell is essentially set in stone by this teaser even if his Toddliness didn't spell it out himself.

Sentinel's the name of both a kingdom and city in the Redguards' province. The inclusion of an elder scroll in the teaser and the quote from Yazar also lend credence to the Verge report's claim that the game will make a big thing out of unravelling secrets linked to the provenance of these mysterious bits of paper. As for the quote's yammering of lost futures and undone victories, I'll venture to speculate that it could turn out to be reference to the player character thwarting a Thalmor victory, since Skyrim seemed to set up the elves as being on the verge of conquering Tamriel as the Cyrodillic empire fractured and fell.

That may or may not be the case, but we do know for sure that this teaser likely means a huge downturn in use of the header image below. It's eight years old, pulled from The Elder Scrolls 6's infamous 2018 teaser. All these years on, the game's finally on the way. You've served us well, screengrab of some hills. Talos guide you to wherever less regularly used images go.

Elder Scrolls teasing aside, it's worth bearing in mind that Bethesda parent company Microsoft have spent the majority of this year gutting their workforce with mass layoffs and studio ditching. Microsoft are also still currently subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

#4087. Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3 has been announced, marking another attempt at a free-to-play team game after Gundam Evolution's unfortunate fate

Bandai Namco have released the initial announcement trailer for Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3, a free-to-play team action game and a sequel to 2018's Battle Operation 2. The trailer is very, very pretty, showing off Gundam units clashing in large-scale battles and infantry fighting beneath the colossal mechas' feet (kinda like Titanfall, in having both human and mecha players in the same match). I'm sadly not yet enough of a true Gundam fan to recognise many of these units on sight other than the RX-78-2, but there's a real variety shown off here.

MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM GUNDAM BATTLE OPERATION 3　Announcement Trailer Watch on YouTube

While there's no release date specified in the trailer, Bandai Namco have confirmed that there will be a network test in Japan through November 20th-22nd, with an open network test planned for the future (thanks, Gematsu).

Following the fate of Gundam Evolution, a 2022 attempt at a hero shooter featuring Gundam units, it's nice to see another shot at taking the Gundam series into a team format. Evolution suffered from the all-too-common trappings of heavy microtransaction inclusion, with several playable Gundam units with unique abilities only available through paying real cash. It was rightly criticised for this, and since Bandai Namco seemed to have had high hopes for the revenue it could make from said microtransactions, the lack of money made meant it shut down just a year later.

Contrastingly, from what I can see, Gundam Battle Operation 2 was received fairly well on its release. While little is actually known about the third game at this point, let's hope it has a better chance than the series' last big release. I will quickly note that the trailer does close with a "*Some content may require purchase" note, so it'll likely have some form of microtransaction in itself — hopefully not to the same degree as Evolution. And, while we're on the topic of Gundam, there's also 2027's Gundam Rogue Orbit, a drastically different game that seems closer to a Devil May Cry-esque action title (though, unlike Battle Operation 3, will begin life as a timed exclusive to PS5). Now, if we could get a Gundam game that plays something like Armored Core, and god willing a proper PC release, I would be a very happy girl.

#4086. Mini Review: Barbie Rewind (PS5) - Fab Outer Layer Brings This Retro Ensemble Together

Version Reviewed: PS5 (Standard) / European

The only Barbie title I've played, prior to Barbie Rewind, is a PC game named Fashion Designer, in which you choose clothes based on particular themes, then apply patterns, accessories, and colours. You could print them out and put them on real Barbie dolls — a nice idea.

Sadly, Fashion Designer isn't among the games included in Barbie Rewind, but what is in this retro compilation is similarly simple and enjoyable, for the most part.

16 old school games starring the iconic doll feature here, from 1991's simply-named platformer Barbie all the way to 2007's Barbie as the Island Princess, basically a handful of mini-games.

Some of the included titles don't hold up particularly well nowadays, but it's still interesting to see the gaming legacy of the character, which spans a surprisingly wide range of experiences. There are sports, horse riding, detective adventures, and more.

While it's obviously great to have all these games gathered — especially with the inclusion of the previously unreleased Barbie Vacation Adventure — the best thing about Barbie Rewind is actually the way it's packaged.

You can play the classic games at any time, but tying it all together is an in-game DreamHouse that you can freely decorate as you unlock more items.

Completing basic challenges in the retro titles unlocks new rooms as well as more furniture and accessories, giving you somewhere to return to and kit out as you see fit.

It's a really neat way to encourage you to play all the games, making the collection feel nicely cohesive. It's also an entertaining thing to noodle around with in its own right, with hundreds of items and several rooms to decorate.

The way it's presented reminds me of Unpacking; it doesn't have that game's wonderful wordless storytelling, but placing down objects just how you want them has a similar appeal here.

On top of that, there's the Catalog, which is the museum style mode with lots of old documents and materials to look through regarding Barbie as well as the games themselves.

It's another great effort from Digital Eclipse, and I think going the extra mile with the DreamHouse really lifts the whole thing. If you're nostalgic for Barbie games or are just curious about their history, this is a lovely way to experience them.

#4085. 'Generally Favourable' Review Scores For Trio Of Xbox Game Pass Launch Titles

Decent scores for Warhammer Survivors, Tanuki: Pon's Summer, and Football Manager 27

Three games from November's Xbox Game Pass lineup are launching today, and they're already picking up some pretty decent review scores.

Warhammer Survivors, Tanuki: Pon's Summer, and Football Manager 27 Console are available for Ultimate and PC Game Pass members today. It's a pretty busy day for the service, especially if you're interested in playing all three, so we decided to do quick review roundup of them all.

This way you can see what the critics are saying and maybe decide which game you fancy playing first. So, here's what reviews are saying about the three new Xbox Game Pass titles:

"You’ll find yourself smiling as you log dozens and dozens of hours in this installment of Football Manager, which takes a leap forward from last year’s revolutionary release, offering a more polished, streamlined game with even faster processing speeds. The loss of official team name licenses is becoming a serious problem, but once you get past that hurdle, Football Manager 27 offers a well-rounded managerial experience that’s increasingly optimized and satisfying." - Google Translate

"Football Manager 2027 marks a strong return to previous highs, following the stumbles last year, with the standout feature being the impressive and engaging changes to the tactics system, enhanced by greater control and noticeable feedback. Fans of the series should, and will, enjoy it, and it will make a good move forward for those who have been sticking with FM24."

"Football Manager 27 has finally regained its appeal with improved controls and greater tactical depth. Unfortunately, AI glitches and missing features continue to be a nuisance."

"We have not yet returned to the levels of Football Manager 2024: the interface needs to strike a more convincing balance between accessibility and efficiency, while the game engine remains the primary obstacle to the project’s full success. It is difficult to overlook certain player behaviors when the rest of the game encourages an ever-greater focus on tactical preparation."

"Tanuki: Pon's Summer is a charming, nostalgia-filled adventure that captures the magic of childhood summers through BMX exploration, quirky characters, and an impressive variety of mini-games. Its vibrant rural Japanese setting and fantastic soundtrack make every delivery feel like a new discovery. While limited BMX tricks and underdeveloped shrine customization leave room for improvement, Pon's summer adventure is a heartfelt experience that's easy to get lost in."

"This adorable adventure has clearly been made with a lot of care and attention, and that shines through in the engaging cycling gameplay and the endearing characters. Its mini-games do their best to hide the fact that the game's mainly a series of fetch quests, but the love that's gone into making it is contagious."

"Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is the rare cosy game that truly lives up to its premise, balancing both whimsical and snarky humour, alongside gameplay that manages to keep you moving just enough to hide its more shallow mechanics. Combined with a surprisingly generous array of content and impressive presentation, this is a Game Pass launch well worth checking out, even if a few wobbly wheels may disrupt your journey."

"TANUKI: Pon’s Summer is seriously charming, and that goes a long way to papering over some of the issues I had with it. If you loved Pon as much as I did then you'll definitely enjoy your summer with him."

"Warhammer Survivors is as addictive as Vampire Survivors, but has some unique twists that keep the experience interesting. It's also nearly flawless on the Steam Deck."

"All in all, Warhammer Survivors perfectly melds Games Workshop's property with poncle's timeless formula, resulting in another exceptional roguelike experience."

Mini Review Warhammer Survivors (PS5) - Absurdly Addictive Crossover Is a Match Made in Bullet Hell

"If you’re looking for the next twist on the Vampire Survivors formula and the idea of a Warhammer spin-off excites you, absolutely do not skip Warhammer Survivors – it’s on virtually every platform, it isn’t demanding on the system and and it’s quite cheap. It’s full or Warhammer goodness from two universes, and it introduces various twists the make the combat more varied and engaging. A slow start and the game being a lot less varied and content-filled than Poncle‘s masterpiece do limit the game’s long-term potential, but Warhammer‘s survivors-like romp is a blast, one that will keep me glued to the screen for quite some time even after this review."

"Considering these examples, Warhammer Survivors is a few days late and dollars short, albeit at a budget price. For those of you who’ve fully rinsed Vampire Survivors… Well, first off, that’s simply an impressive feat; well done. But secondly, here are another 40 heroes to max out, with hundreds of objectives to clear. Consider your bullet heaven buffet fully restocked."

There you have it, folks! Decent scores all around for today's Xbox Game Pass launch titles. Of the three, Football Manager 27 appears to have impressed the most, but only time will tell if that remains the case. Warhammer Survivors is pulling in mixed scores, although there's still a chance its score could climb a smidge.

It seems that Ruaridh Mollica is hopeful for a Young Avengers movie

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ruaridh Mollica is absolutely down for a Young Avengers movie... especially after the big reveal in the final episode of VisionQuest.

Warning: there are massive spoilers for VisionQuest episode 8 ahead!

In the season finale of VisionQuest, Tommy finally reunites with his brother Billy – and it all becomes a very sweet family reunion. After Vision saves the world from a vengeful Ultron (again), Billy appears and is pulled in for a rather heartwarming group hug.

"Do the words 'young' and 'Avengers' mean anything to you?" Iman Vellani asked Mollica during a special VisionQuest episode of the Marvel podcast she hosts with Frank Alvarez.

"They mean a dream I would love to come true," he replied.

Now that Tommy aka Speed has arrived, and has finally teamed up with Billy aka Wiccan, this means the following comic book-accurate Young Avengers members are currently in the MCU: Speed, Wiccan, Kamala Khan aka Ms. Marvel, Kate Bishop, Cassie Lang, Skaar, Lisa Molinari, and America Chavez. I think those are enough characters for a standalone movie, wouldn't you say?

There is also the fact that the extra post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest implies that Tommy and Billy could be in Avengers: Doomsday, as the scene sees Wanda resurrected by Doom... but seemingly put under his spell. There's a Young Avengers comic book arc where Wanda goes missing, loses her memory, and becomes Doom's bride. But we'll just have to see on December 18.

VisionQuest is streaming now in its entirety on Disney Plus. For even more, check out our VisionQuest review or our VisionQuest ending explained.

#4083. Venom-toothed Noxious Terminids are soon to infest Helldivers 2, and it's your noble job to sterilise the galaxy for Super Earth

Helldivers 2 isn't slowing down any time soon, and according to Edwin's recent interview with Arrowhead CCO Johan Pilestedt, it'll continue to be Arrowhead's main priority for the future. As if Helldivers 2 wasn't full of enough horrors for our brave Super Earth Helldivers to shoot at for the betterment of galactic democracy, its next update is due to add an entirely new Terminid subspecies, the Noxious Terminids.

First up on are the Noxious Scavengers. These horrible little (see: huge) things skitter around at high speed and are loaded with deadly poison, but are thankfully at least fragile. Liberal use of area-of-effect weapons such as flamethrowers, explosives and flamethrowers are recommended to avoid being overrun by these horse-sized insects. Then there's the Noxious Spewer, which is not only fast like its smaller brethren despite its larger size, but also equipped with a web projectile which locks a Helldiver in place, vulnerable to a fatal bite. Oh, and if you dare shoot its soft underbelly, it violently explodes, with the same web fluid covering a wide area around it. The poison inflicted by these creatures' bites is a new damage over time effect that can blur vision, slow movement, eat away at your health, and make you fear this may be the end for you — so it's a bit like getting the flu (get your jabs!)

HELLDIVERS™ 2 | A Cleaner Galaxy Starts With You Watch on YouTube

This update also makes the change that bug caves can be found across many more worlds across the galaxy, leading troopers down tunnels with limited visibility and claustrophobic dead ends. Super Earth's propaganda, sorry, I mean, guidance, describes the galactic sterilisation program quite simply: locate the invasive species, identify the horrific monsters at the barrel of your flamethrower, and sterilise (burn to cinders). The guidance also, hilariously, includes the line: "Super Earth reminds you that ammunition is cheaper than antivenom." Now, get out there and rid our beautiful democracy of this vile pestilence.

#4082. Danganronpa Creator Says Physical Game Production Is Reliant On Day-One Patches

"We barely pass platform certification requirements"

Kazutaka Kodaka, creator of Danganronpa and The Hundred Line, has made a pretty incredible admission regarding the production of physical games.

His comments were made during a roundtable discussion at the SKY31 Convention Seoul (thanks, Kotaku) during which he explains how developer Too Kyo Games is able to meet ongoing demand for physical games, particularly in Japan.

Essentially, the production of physical games requires the original master to be submitted much earlier than digital titles. This is to account for the extended time required to pack the items, especially if it's a collector's edition.

So Kodaka-san confessed that the studio often submits builds that, in his words, shouldn't be played by anyone. He operates under the assumption that everyone has access to the internet these days and is therefore able to download a day-one patch to bring the game up to an acceptable standard.

“Honestly, we approach it with the mindset of finalizing the master via patches. Collector’s editions in North America or Europe take an enormous amount of time to pack with figures, so the master submission deadline is absurdly early.

"To be frank, we sometimes submit builds where we think, ‘No one should ever play it in this state.’ We barely pass platform certification requirements and release it while believing no one plays games without an internet connection these days.”

He goes on to jokingly say "I’m not sure if I should be making such risky confessions in a venue like this". To be fair though, it sounds like Kodaka is merely being honest and open about a practice that is widely adopted by the industry at large.

Hell, even Ocarina of Time received a day-one patch. Granted, this was primarily to enable connection to Zelda Notes, but if you bought the physical and couldn't update it for whatever reason, you wouldn't be able to use this feature.

Kodaka's next project is Danganronpa 2x2 for the Switch and Switch 2. In somewhat related news, it was revealed earlier this year that the collector's editions on Switch 2 would no longer come with a full cartridge, with Spike Chunsoft instead opting for a Game-Key Card.

#4081. Frostpunk 2's The Surge DLC keeps the wintery apocalypse and adds in faction-clash-inducing electricity and sets a seasonally appropriate December release date

For the time being, the world of Frostpunk remains a hypothetical, even if it's one that seems just that little bit more likely than I'd like it to be given who's in charge of the world. But at the very least, there are pockets of hope to be found in Frostpunk 2, namely with its newly revealed next bit of DLC, The Surge, a name that has been bequeathed to it for incredibly obvious reasons. Oh, you need me to explain them? Fiiiiine.

You and your probably not so merry band of survivors have been trekking across the UK, when you end up at a "mysterious valley." Apparently some rumours have been going round about a "marvel left behind by history’s greatest mind - a relic with the potential to reshape the world itself." So you go off to look for it, and it essentially seems like this relic lets you use a whole bunch of electricity. Only, despite how useful this is for automating a bunch of work, various factions disagree over how it should be used, "while the secrets hidden within the valley prove far more difficult to uncover than anyone expected."

In terms of what you should expect from this DLC, for starters there's a new scenario to check out "set in an entirely new region, far beyond the borders explored in Frostpunk 2 so far." This relic is also implied to have come from the mind of one Nikola Tesla, you know, the electricity guy. There'll apparently be ways to utilise the Great Storm that's ruined the planet to "turn catastrophic whiteouts into valuable, harvested and stored resources." And you'll have some hidden treasures to find and mysterious to uncover in various nearby caves and ruins.

All sounds neat enough! And it's not too far away either. The Surge is currently slated for a seasonally appropriate December 14th release date. Let's hope no real world environmental disasters get in the way of that, 'ey? While you wait for it, you can wishlist the DLC on Steam.

#4080. Square Enix Sees Huge Increase in Digital Game Sales, Upping Its Financial Forecast

Much like Capcom, Square Enix is seeing a significant surge in digital game sales, as opposed to physical, with the latter now in steady decline.

In fact, Square Enix's latest financial report is pretty eye-opening. It makes for a positive assessment of the company — something of a rarity over the last several years — and it's primarily down to the aforementioned increase in digital purchases.

The publisher reveals that digital sales have practically exploded, jumping from 5.83 million to 8.19 million year-on-year. It cites healthy numbers for Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth's Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox ports, and The Adventures of Elliot — the action RPG that was released back in the summer.

In total, a whopping 89% of all Square Enix's sales were digital over the last six months, while physical sales dropped from 1.09 million units to 1.01.

So while there's still some demand for boxed games, the slice of the pie is only getting smaller.

All of this has led to the Japanese company upping its financial forecast for the rest of the fiscal year, going from ¥298,000 million to ¥310,000 million. While not a massive jump, it's still a good sign, given the publisher's recent struggles.

Of course, all eyes will now be on Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, which launches on the 8th April. It'll be the first game in the trilogy to release on multiple platforms — a move that Square Enix thinks could make a big difference after Rebirth couldn't come close to matching Remake's initial sales.

What do you make of Square Enix's current situation? Is the publisher finally on the up? Wait for some digital discounts in the comments section below.

#4079. My Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy's entire story so far will get you FF7 Revelation-ready

Now over 100 hours in, catch up on the events of the first two parts of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is the third and final instalment of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy that reimagines the 1997 PS1 JRPG classic while incorporating the wider universe known as The Compilation of Final Fantasy 7 (which includes spin-offs like PSP's Crisis Core: Final Fantasy 7, and even movies like Advent Children).

While there's still time to catch up on the first two parts ahead of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's impending April 8, 2027 release, which will conclude the saga, you've come to the right place if you're after a condensed catch up on the story so far of Cloud Strife and co's fight to save the planet, and how this retelling also deviates from the original game. It goes without saying that there will be spoilers ahead. If you're in need of a refresher without making time for hundreds of hours re-adventuring, or just want to catch the climax of Cloud and Sephiroth's ultimate clash, then we've got you covered.

If you're ready to make like a chocobo, then let's go!

With the remake trilogy drawing to a close early 2027, we get ready for the epic conclusion with our Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Big Preview across hands-on impressions, dev access, and deep dives into the whole adventure so far.

We kick off with Final Fantasy 7 Remake, which covers just the original game's opening section in Midgar, a multi-tiered dystopian metropolis controlled by fascist megacorporation Shinra. Just like the original Final Fantasy 7, it opens with protagonist Cloud, a former member of SOLDIER, Shinra's elite military, who's now working as a mercenary for eco-terrorist group Avalanche. Their mission is to blow up Mako Reactor 1 in order to disrupt Shinra's activities of harvesting Mako energy, which they believe is sucking the planet's life force dry.

With the bombing mission a success – though the remake deviates from the original by making Avalanche's bomb a dud while President Shinra actually sets off the real explosion that's far deadlier than intended – the group's leader Barret Wallace feels emboldened to target Mako Reactor 5, with Cloud also joining the mission, alongside his childhood friend Tifa Lockhart from the Sector 7 undercity's slums.

Between these missions, we also see how else Final Fantasy 7 Remake expands and deviates from the original game, as we learn of Avalanche member Jessie' backstory as a theater actress who leaves behind her stage career after her father falls into a coma due to Mako poisoning, while Cloud has visions of the game's true threat, Sephiroth, and a chance encounter with flower girl Aerith Gainsborough is interrupted by the presence of mysterious hooded specters.

However, the Mako Reactor 5 mission goes awry, leading to Cloud being separated from Avalanche and crashing into a church in the Sector 5 slums where he once again encounters Aerith, who is being pursued by Shinra's covert ops Turks unit. Aerith joins Cloud on his way back to Sector 7 when they notice a carriage passing by, which Tifa is inside, heading to the manor of Don Corneo, a slumlord in Sector 5, home to the seedy entertainment district of Wall Market.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

After an elaborate makeover for both Cloud and Aerith to infiltrate Don Corneo's manor to rescue Tifa, they learn from the Don that Shinra plans to drop the Sector 7 plate onto the slums below to destroy Avalanche, regardless of all the innocent people who would also be killed. Despite their best efforts, the plate drops, causing huge destruction and casualties, including the death of Avalanche members Biggs and Jessie, while Aerith allows herself to be captured by Shinra in exchange for the safety of Marlene, Barret's daughter.

Resolved to rescue Aerith, Cloud, Barrett, and Tifa infiltrate Shinra's headquarters before its head scientist Hojo can experiment on her. Aerith is revealed to be the last descendant of the Cetra (also known as the Ancients), a mystical precursor race connected to the Lifestream, which Shinra wants to exploit in order to gain access to the Mako-rich 'Promised Land'.

During Aerith's rescue and the group's escape, they are joined by Red XIII, a dog-like creature who has also been a captive of Hojo's experiments, while President Shinra is killed by Sephiroth, only to be quickly succeeded by his son Rufus.

As Cloud leads the team with a motorcycle to escape the rest of Shinra's forces and reach Midgar's outskirts, it culminates in a confrontation with Sephiroth and the hooded specters that Red XIII calls Whispers. Their presence throughout the story have been to essentially act as arbiters of fate, which in a meta twist, ensures that events play out just like they did in the original story of Final Fantasy 7. This explains their intervention in moments where fate almost diverges, such as ensuring that Cloud spares Turk member Reno during their fight, that he doesn't leave Avalanche high and dry on the fifth Mako reactor mission, or that Barret survives what should have been a fatal stabbing from Sephiroth.

In a battle against the whispers and Sephiroth, the team successfully defy fate, and as they leave Midgar, we see implications of how the universe has split into into alternate timelines, with one where Biggs and Jessie survived the falling of the Sector 7 plate, and another where another SOLDIER named Zack – someone Aerith had been previously in love with – survives an attack by Shinra forces and is seen carrying a wounded Cloud to Midgar (he famously dies in both the original's flashback scenes, and PSP sequel Crisis Core).

While much of FF7 Remake kept us guessing as to how close events would hew to the original game, and what role the Whispers functioned, this striking ending blows the doors wide open – leaving many to wonder if the sequel would have much in common with the original events at all.

Alongside the events of Final Fantasy 7 Remake, Intermission follows Yuffie, a young ninja who has come to Midgar on a mission from the interim Wutai government – Shinra's arch rival – to steal Shinra's 'Ultimate Materia' with the help of her partner Sonon and a local Avalanche cell, where it also emerges that Barret's Avalanche is considered a more radical fringe breakaway faction from a broader Avalanche organization.

Yuffie and Sonon infiltrate a lab underneath Shinra HQ where they battle against Scarlet, Shinra's head of weapon research, as well as top-secret military organization Deepground, including one of their leaders Nero the Sable. While the mission ends in failure as there turns out to be no 'Ultimate Materia', and Sonon sacrifices himself to ensure Yuffie's escape, this ordeal gives the young Wutai ninja the resolve to find likeminded allies to help her bring down Shinra.

Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth begins by exploring more of the first entry's alternate timeline split through Zack, where the Avalanche members are seen wounded and taken captive while Aerith is comatose. Zack manages to take both her and Cloud to hide out at her mother Elmyra's house. It's gradually revealed that in this timeline, the planet's Mako has already been fully depleted as people brace for the imminent end of the world.

Back in Remake's original timeline, Cloud and the party have left behind Midgar and arrive in the town of Kalm where he relays his past with Sephiroth when both were assigned to investigate a Mako reactor in Cloud's hometown of Nibelheim five years ago. During this mission, Sephiroth suffered a mental breakdown after learning that he was artificially created from the cells of an extra-terrestrial life-form called Jenova, his identity crisis resulting in the massacre and destruction of Nibelheim before returning to the reactor to recover the body of his 'mother'.

The party decides to pursue Sephiroth by following the trail of 'black robes', former Shinra test subjects, who Cloud believes will lead them to Sephiroth. They journey across the wider world, including the Shinra-controlled port city of Junon during an inauguration parade for Shinra's new president Rufus; the sun-kissed Costa Del Sol where Aerith and Tifa want to let their hair down but Hojo is also using the black robes as part of his heinous experiments; Barret's hometown of Mt. Corel where the group learns he is blamed for the explosion of its Mako reactor; the Gold Saucer filled with minigames and home to the popular play Loveless; Zack's hometown of Gongaga; Red XIII's hometown of Cosmo Canyon, where it's revealed his real name is Nanaki and despite his deep voice, his age is developmentally equivalent to a 15 or 16 year-old human; there's even a return to Nibelheim, which Shinra has eerily rebuilt in its entirety.

Along the way, new members also join the party, including Wutai ninja Yuffie, remote-controlled robot cat Cait Sith, pilot Cid Highwind who owns the dual-propeller airplane the Tiny Bronco, and the vampiric beast-transforming ex-Turk Vincent Valentine (the latter two are non-playable in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth). They also encounter several appearances of Weapons, gigantic guardians that act as part of the Planet's self-defense. Despite defeating the Arbiter of Fate, the whispers also return but in new variants, with white whispers allying themselves with the Planet, while the black ones are aiding Sephiroth's plans. The party soon learns that his ultimate plan is to use the Black Materia to summon Meteor to destroy the Planet.

This culminates in a race between Cloud's party and Shinra through the Temple of the Ancients in search of the Black Materia, all while Wutai openly declares war on Shinra. Despite the party's successful efforts in securing the Black Materia, Sephiroth takes control of Cloud's mind, forcing him to hand it over, and explains his plans of 'Reunion', which would forcibly fuse the alternate universes together into a paradise he can rule over.

In the ensuing chaos, Aerith goes it alone to try and stop Sephiroth, and the party traces her to the Forgotten Capital, an ancient Cetran City. They are blocked by a horde of whispers from entering the temple where Aerith is, but a tear opens enough for Cloud to go through, where he finds Aerith attempting to pray for help from the Planet to stop Sephiroth.

Whereas in the original story, Sephiroth tries to force Cloud to kill her, this time the whispers try to manipulate Cloud to use his Buster Sword, though he resists. Sephiroth descends from the sky to get the job done himself, and while Cloud blocks and disarms him, a distortion in the timeline makes it so that Sephiroth does kill Aerith, sending her White Materia into the water. While this causes the whispers to disperse, allowing the rest of the party to catch and fight Jenova like in the original game, Cloud is separated and finds his timeline converging with Zack's.

Zack's timeline, meanwhile, has been fracturing into multiple threads, each based on a different decision he makes, including trying to save a version of Biggs who survived Remake's destruction of Sector 7. Ultimately, Zack also comes face to face with Sephiroth, temporarily having Cloud assist as they fight their common foe across universes, while Aerith from an alternate timeline comes to Cloud's aid in the final battle. Although the fight forces Sephiroth to retreat, in the current timeline, the party members mourn Aerith's death, even though Cloud still seems to be able to see her.

As the party lick their wounds and continue pursuing Sephiroth on Cid's Tiny Bronco, Cloud discovers he still has the Black Materia, which he fuses into the Buster Sword, while he is also able to see a black rift in the sky that the others cannot. As he says goodbye to Aerith's ghost, who stays behind, Cloud vows to stop Sephiroth. This time, it's not just about stopping him from destroying the Planet and controlling the Lifestream like it was in the PS1 game, but from controlling all realities and timelines in the many universes of Final Fantasy 7.

What will happen next in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation remains to be seen, especially when it comes to how closely it'll stay to the final arc of the PS1 game. If you're curious to know more, join me later in the week as I unravel 8 story threads I hope Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will resolve, and continue exploring this epic saga's narrative.

Fancy more fantasy? Check out our best RPGs and best JRPGs rankings for more adventures worth unsheathing your Buster Sword to tackle.

#4078. Marathon To Add New Co-Op Roguelite Mode, Social Spaces, And Other Major Features In December

It's beginning to look a lot like Destiny

Bungie isn't prepared to let its extraction shooter go quietly. Instead, Marathon's upcoming 'Symbiosis' update arrives on December 8, bringing a whole host of new PvE and PvP modes. Having just finished watching the new gameplay trailer above, I've got to say, It's giving off plenty of Destiny vibes.

I'm a big, big fan of Marathon, but that's not to say I don't think the game needs a shake-up. It clearly needs something to keep things ticking along. I can't help but feel extremely hyped now that Bungie has shared a first look at all the new content coming next month.

The most interesting addition of the bunch is 'Limbo': a new social space. This is where runners can hang out, chat, test weapons at the firing range and challenge each other in the duelling pit. It reminds me of The Tower from Destiny 2.

Social spaces play a huge role in fostering a sense of community in games, and Bungie knows all about that. Just look at the time Destiny players gathered at The Tower en masse to mourn the passing of Lance Reddick, the voice of Commander Zavala.

Beyond that, 'Expedition' is a new co-op PvE roguelite mode. No PvP, just you and your crew going against new threats. PlayStation.Blog shared an official description of the the new mode:

"Expedition: Phase 1 of a new PvE-only mode built around a three-run series. Play solo or with a crew, face new combat and environmental challenges without PvP threats, and use Flash Boosts to shape your build during a run."

If battling it out against other runners is more your style, Marathon is getting it's first PvP mode, Deathmatch (Beta) pitting quick 3v3 matches against one another. Personally, I think this is a great way to let players get used to the game's arsenal of weapons and gadgets without the time commitment that comes with extraction.

There are a few other new bits and bobs coming to Marathon in December, including a new runner shell, which we'll cover below:

To coincide with the Symbiosis update, Bungie will also be hosting an Open Play Week starting December 8, allowing new players to download and play Marathon for free.

#4077. Play as water and rain on wildfires in Atuel, a short, free game about the power and vulnerability of nature

Well, have you played Atuel? If not, you can do so within the next hour - it's a tiny, free, 25-minute walking sim, albeit one with little actual walking on account of you playing most of it as a river. More of a running sim, really.

Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives.

Technically, Atuel calls itself a "documentary game", and not without justification. While its sweeping Patagonian landscapes are rendered with a dreamy otherworldliness, and certain moments are downright mystic, the whole watery journey is based directly on the Atuel River that runs through western Argentina. As you drift downhill, taking control of water, clouds, and the local wildlife, you'll hear real-life scientists and historians monologuing on the Atuel and its relationship with the human cultures it's nourished. Mercifully, these are delivered with thoughtfulness as well as earnestness, maintaining the game's contemplative atmosphere without making it sound like the audio guide to a museum of Birmingham canals.

A few bends in, Atuel also takes on the climate crisis, directing you away from the soothing freshwater and into wildfires and parched riverbeds. I'd say this was preaching to the choir, at least for anyone who a) desires a functioning planet and b) learned about the water cycle in primary school, but then it isn't really preaching. Rather, developers Matajuegos weave between the beauty of the Earth and the need to protect it quite gracefully, and end their river tour on a more hopeful note than its darker moments may have intimated.

There's plenty else to leave an outsized impression in your memory matter: the understated, naturally-textured soundtrack, for instance, or the patiently gradual zoom-outs that slowly unveil the Andes' wild splendour. For me, and without wanting to undermine the importance or the accuracy of Atuel's environmental point, it was mainly just nice – therapeutic, even – to float through its gorgeous, surreal scenery like a cloud. And sometimes, as one. You can download it for free from Steam and Itch, with a pay-what-you-want option on the latter.

#4075. Silica, an FPS and RTS hybrid that mixes a smidge of Dune and Helldivers together, has left early access and entered 1.0

The concept of fusing an RTS and an FPS always sounds like a fun one, and since 2023 Martin Melichárek has been trying to make a new take on the combination under the watchful eye of DayZ devs Bohemia Interactive through Silica. Today marks the day that Silica leaves early access and enters 1.0, fully fleshing out its hybrid and mish mash of Dune's Arrakis and Helldivers' Terminids.

Digging into Silica a touch more deeply, it is a sci-fi shooter set on a planet where there's a fancy resource you're trying to mine that definitely isn't the spice. There are two warring factions competing for said resource, when, uh oh! Some bug-ish, giant aliens aren't very happy you're doing all that. So, you can either join the fray on the ground with some classic first-person shooting alongside your friends, or you can take the role of commander and dictate your artillery from above.

The 1.0 update obviously comes with a few additions, namely the Centauri Campaign, a "story-driven single-player experience set in the war for Baltarus. It opens with a cinematic intro and features fully voiced mission briefings and in-game dialogue. Between missions, a 3D planetary globe tracks the war as territory changes hands." Commanding your army should be a better experience now too, with the ability to "arrange units into formations, issue more precise movement and attack orders, and quickly select all units of the same type. Improved AI targeting and vehicle movement also help your armies operate more effectively in large-scale battles."

Beyond that, 1v1 matchmaking has been added in, where you can fight against another commander. The Steam Workshop sandbox tools have been expanded for building your own scenarios and sharing them with others. And there are a whole bunch of bug fixes, quality-of-life improvements and additions, and more. You can read about some of those in more detail in this handy little blog post. If you like what Silica is putting down, then you can pick it up on Steam.
